props.title: Which configuration fits which kind of event.
props.lede: Most people book by the kind of event first and the sound second, so here’s the roster sorted that way. Every act named here has a page of its own.

rows.term: A cocktail hour, a dinner, or background music
rows.text: A solo guitarist, a singer and guitarist, a Spanish guitarist, a jazz duo, an acoustic duo, a pianist or Last Consulate, one musician on upright bass and guitar over downtempo electronics, all quiet enough that your guests keep talking. In December the Christmas jazz trio plays the season at the same volume.

rows.term: A party with a dance floor
rows.text: A trio or a quartet. Tejas Singh and Tony Medina both grow from a small build to a four piece on one contract, and the Americana band, the yacht rock band, the soul and R&B band and the funk band are each a floor with a different sound on it. Live band karaoke is the one where your people take the mic.

rows.term: A DJ, on its own or after the band
rows.text: The DJ is open format, and it books alone or after any band on the roster through the same sound system, on the same contract.

rows.term: A set piece your guests watch
rows.text: Dirty Flamenco, Changes Jazz Trio with a saxophone added, René Moffatt playing his own songs, Your Bird Can Sing for a crowd that sings along, and Firstwater for a sound bath at an offsite or a wellness day.

An acoustic or Spanish guitarist for the ceremony, a duo for the cocktail hour and the DJ for the floor, on one contract. The weddings page walks through all three, and the wedding jazz band covers the whole day in one style.
A jazz duo or a guitarist for senior living, a memorial or a Sunday brunch, the Beatles sing-along for a community afternoon, and a daytime sound bath. The daytime page has each of them.

props.html: Every act plays Denver, the Front Range and the mountain towns, and travel past the metro is quoted as its own line. What live music costs in this market is on the pricing page.

lanes.title: The configurations, smallest first.
lanes.lede: Each one is a sound at a size, a jazz duo or a yacht rock band, played by working musicians matched to your date. Open any of them for what it sounds like, the sizes it books and the events it suits.

lanes.title: The named acts.

props._notes:
Two lanes, 2026-09-23. The roster grid used to list every act in file
     order, named and spec'd mixed, with the hand-typed configuration index
     fourteen phone screens further down and five configuration pages that
     were on no card at all. Now the configurations come first, compact and
     smallest first, and the named acts follow with their footage. Both lanes
     render from acts.json (`lane`, see its _lanes_note), so a new act joins
     the right lane on the next build with nothing to type here.

     Filter UI ships hidden and acts.js unhides it, so with script off every
     act on the roster is still on the page. The filter is a class toggle
     over data attributes rendered by build.py, never a re-render, and it
     works across both lanes; a lane with nothing left in it hides its own
     heading. The page opens pre-filtered from a query string
     (?occasion=weddings, ?size=duo, ?genre=jazz, ?night=party), which is how
     an occasion page can point at the acts that suit it.

Daniel's disclaimer, 2026-09-19, on the page that lists every act and
         size. The footer carries the same sentence sitewide.

props.html: Stage lighting and a dedicated engineer are optional add-ons. Travel outside the metro, holiday weekends and New Year's Eve are also available as market priced.
The operational questions, from substitutions to decibel caps, are on the full FAQ list.

items.q: What's the difference between a "named act" and a configuration?
items.a: A named act is booked under its name, and that specific sound and presence comes with the booking: Tejas Singh, Tony Medina, René Moffatt, Dirty Flamenco, Changes Jazz Trio, Your Bird Can Sing, Last Consulate and Firstwater. A configuration is a format we spec by instrumentation, size and repertoire, like a jazz duo or a yacht rock band, and the contract names the configuration. Both kinds have a page of their own.

items.q: Which size do most private parties book?
items.a: A duo or a trio. A duo plays arrival and dinner at a volume people talk across, and a trio of guitar, bass and drums fills a floor without a stage. For a company party in a ballroom the quartet is the dance floor size, and a duo through dinner with the DJ after it covers both halves of the night on one contract.

items.q: Can a booking start small and grow through the evening?
items.a: Yes. Tejas Singh starts as a duo and finishes as a quartet on one contract and one load-in, the jazz duo becomes a trio with drums played with brushes, and the DJ takes over from any band through the same sound system.

items.q: Do you publish prices for the acts?
items.a: No. What live music costs in this market, figure by figure with the source each one came from, is on the pricing page, and we price a specific night when you send the date, the venue and the guest count.

Denver, Boulder, Colorado Springs and Fort Collins, and the mountain towns: Vail, Beaver Creek, Aspen, Breckenridge, Telluride, Steamboat Springs, Winter Park and Crested Butte. Travel outside the metro and a night's lodging past the passes are quoted as their own lines on the contract.
